description_full: Versamet Royalties Corporation operates as metals royalty and streaming company, engages in the acquiring and managing royalties, streams, and other similar interests on metals and mining operations and projects in Peru, the United States, Africa, and Canada. It explores for silver, gold, copper, graphite, lead, uranium, zinc, and molybdenum metals. Versamet Royalties Corporation was formerly known as Sandbox Royalties Corp. and changed its name to Versamet Royalties Corporation in June 2024. The company was incorporated in 2011 and is based in Vancouver, Canada.
ceo_bio: Mr. Daniel  O'Flaherty | Chief Executive Officer & Director | Age 43 | Compensation: $565,870 (FY2025)
financial_summary: Versamet Royalties Corporation is a small-cap basic materials business with a $874M market cap on $35M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +233% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +49.9pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -2% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 27%.

The business throws off $17M in free cash flow — roughly 49 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.83× cash conversion.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 13.9× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 0.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 60% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
